title: fix(#6651): a descriptor accessor's .name is not the descriptor slot's name
author: claude
head: 5a31a5e4e898def8a926049c04ba47334331cc30
body:
**Before:** reading a getter out of a property descriptor and asking for its name
gave the wrong answer. `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(obj, Symbol.species).get`
returns the installed getter, but `getter.name` answered `"get"` — the name of the
`PropertyDescriptor.get` declaration slot in `lib.es5.d.ts`, not the function's own
name. A user accessor installed as a named function expression
(`{ get: function realGet() {} }`) read back as `"get"` for the same reason.

**After:** the name comes from the function itself, so the test262 row
`built-ins/Symbol/species/builtin-getter-name.js` passes, and a named accessor
reports its own name. An anonymous accessor still reports `"get"`, which is what
§13.2.5.5 requires.

The §20.2.4.2 `.name` peephole resolves a function's name from its *type* symbol.
That is right for an ordinary function reference and wrong whenever the type symbol
is a declaration artefact rather than the function's own declaration. A new
predicate `nameFoldTypeSymbolIsDeclarationArtefact` names that set explicitly:
TypeScript's `__computed` placeholder (the #5149 cluster B case, previously an
inline test) and the §6.2.6 property-descriptor accessor slot. Declining the fold
costs only the fold — the ordinary property read answers from the closure's own
`$fnmeta` in pure Wasm and via `__extern_get(v, "name")` on the JS host.

**How:** `src/codegen/property-access-dispatch.ts` gains the predicate plus a
second one for the descriptor slot, and `tryLengthAndNameReads` consults it instead
of its old inline `__computed` check. The change is unconditional, not gated on
`--target standalone`, because the JS host was wrong in the same direction.

Measured, not assumed, over an 810-row belt on both axes: **+1 row, LOST 0**
(`built-ins/Symbol/species/builtin-getter-name.js`). Verified by reverting the one
source file and rebuilding all three artifacts — adapter key `229dd26a78e7173f`
reverted, `f8ea30539c389db4` restored, reproduced exactly — which flips 4 of the 7
cases in `tests/issue-6651-b18-descriptor-accessor-name.test.ts`, including the
negative control that asserts a *named* accessor keeps its own name.

The previously recorded diagnosis for this row is disproved in both halves, and the
disproof sits beside the predicate: the descriptor is not synthesised per read (two
reads answer the identical function object), and the split is not static versus
parameter receiver. The real discriminator is whether control flow narrowed the
optional slot's `undefined` away at the `.name` read, which is why only the guarded
spellings (`g && g.name`, `g ? g.name : x`) ever folded.

Eighteenth batch for [#6651](https://js2wasm.loopdive.com/dashboard/issue.html?slug=6651-es2015-standalone-100pct-execution-plan).
